amstar2_items.justification: The research question and eligibility criteria define Population (communities in LMICs per World Bank classification), Intervention (endogenous or exogenous WASH interventions involving community participation across four specified authority/engagement levels), and Outcomes (availability of safe water/sanitation, health/behaviour change, and infrastructure/service longevity), with contextual comparisons structured via realist CMO configurations.

No registered protocol (e.g., PROSPERO) or explicit statement of a written a priori protocol established prior to conducting the review is reported, nor are protocol deviations discussed; the authors describe preparatory reading and iterative realist extraction following RAMESES standards.

The authors justify using a realist synthesis approach and including any study reporting primary quantitative or qualitative data (while excluding books and reviews) so diverse evidence could inform emerging context-mechanism-outcome (CMO) configurations.

Three databases (PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus) were searched across two waves (2010-2020) with research librarian input, listed search terms, and a justification for the 10-year date window; however, grey literature, trial registries, and reference lists were not searched, and the English-only restriction was acknowledged as a limitation rather than methodologically justified.

Full-text eligibility assessment was performed by two reviewers (SN and DD, in consultation with SA), but independent duplicate screening at the title/abstract stage (and whether full texts were assessed independently in duplicate rather than split) is not clearly reported.

Three authors (SN, DD, and SA) independently extracted a pilot sample of 5 randomly selected papers (6.8% of the 73 included studies) to calibrate extraction categories, without reporting quantitative inter-rater agreement (>=80%) or confirming independent duplicate extraction for the remaining 68 studies.
No list of studies excluded after full-text screening (with individual reasons for exclusion) is provided in the article or cited as available in supplemental materials.

Study-level characteristics (populations, sample sizes, study designs, comparators, settings, and follow-up durations) are not tabulated in the main text; p. 5 states that even country and intervention type were placed in an online supplemental appendix.

The authors explicitly state on pp. 3 and 15 that no formal quality or risk-of-bias appraisal was conducted on individual included studies, relying instead on qualitative realist judgements of relevance and rigour.
Sources of research funding for the individual included primary studies are not reported.
No meta-analysis or statistical pooling was performed; the review conducted a qualitative realist synthesis of context-mechanism-outcome configurations.
Because no formal risk-of-bias assessment was undertaken for individual primary studies, study-level risk of bias was not accounted for when interpreting or weighting the synthesis findings.

Explaining heterogeneity in WASH intervention outcomes across settings is the central focus of the realist synthesis, which maps 19 socioeconomic, geographical, and institutional contextual factors across 5 mechanisms to explain why interventions succeed or fail.

The authors declare no competing interests and report their funding grants (Indo-Pacific Centre for Health Security SSHS 74427 and Bloomberg Philanthropies Vibrant Oceans Initiative 53006), explicitly stating that funders had no role in study design, analysis, or publication.

raw_response.methodological_notes: S372 (Nelson et al., 2021) is a theory-driven realist review following RAMESES publication standards rather than a conventional Cochrane/PRISMA effectiveness review. Searches were run across PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus in April 2019 and March 2021 (covering 2010-2020, English peer-reviewed primary studies in LMICs; grey literature excluded), with selection counts reported in the text and Figure 1 yielding 73 included studies across 29 countries. On narrow Criterion 2, the review is borderline: its primary exposure is community participation broadly (including behavioural CLTS shaming, peer diffusion, and hygiene education), but three of its five mechanisms (accountability, market, and ownership) and several of its 19 contextual factors examine local institutional governance rules, committee bylaws and management plans, fines/penalties for non-compliance or water-use limits, user fees/tariff enforcement, decision-making authority, and accountability to government water boards and guidelines. AMSTAR 2 is only borderline-fit for a realist synthesis and yields Critically Low confidence due to critical flaws in Q2 (no registered/a priori protocol), Q7 (no excluded full-text list), Q9 (explicit omission of formal risk-of-bias/quality appraisal in favour of RAMESES relevance/rigour screening), and Q13 (no incorporation of study RoB in interpretation). Although the formal summary table of study countries and intervention types was placed in an online supplemental appendix (hence partial_inline_citations_only), cross-checking all empirical LMIC citations in Table 2 and the Results synthesis (excluding theoretical/methodological citations) recovers all 73 unique included primary studies—including exact reconciliation of two duplicate bibliography entries (Kwangware et al. 2014 listed as both Ref 18 and Ref 93; Ganing et al. 2018 listed as both Ref 82 and Ref 128) and matching the reported regional breakdown (5 Latin American studies and 1 SIDS study).
